slides.heading: Strings Made Up Of Strings
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Tries
slides.narration: Let's solve Strings Made Up Of Strings, a very hard tries problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Return the strings from `strings` that can be built by concatenating two or more strings from `substrings` (reuse allowed).
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Return the strings from strings that can be built by concatenating two or more strings from substrings (reuse allowed). Word-break DP per string.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: A trie of the substrings and memoised splitting determine whether a string decomposes into two or more pieces.
slides.narration: A trie of the substrings and memoised splitting determine whether a string decomposes into two or more pieces.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Word-break DP per string → O(L²) each
slides.narration: Trying every split is exponential. A word-break DP per string is quadratic in its length.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. From each index, walk the trie for word ends
3. Recurse on the rest with memo
slides.narration: Step by step. First, build a trie of substrings. Second, from each index, walk the trie for word ends. Third, recurse on the rest with memo. Fourth, require at least two pieces.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Which strings are built from ≥ 2 substrings?
slides.narration: Which strings can be built from at least two of the substrings?

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Word-break DP per string
slides.narration: For each string, a word-break DP finds whether it splits into dictionary pieces, and how many.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Answer
slides.narration: Strings with at least two pieces qualify.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: For each string we fill pieces from zero, extending when a dictionary substring ends at j, and keep strings with at least two pieces.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n times m squared. Space is O of m plus s.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: A string equal to a single substring doesn't count.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: A trie of the substrings and memoised splitting determine whether a string decomposes into two or more pieces.
